entities.summary: Michael Haddad is a Lebanese professional athlete, social entrepreneur, and climate activist. He was born in 1989 in Beirut, Lebanon, and grew up in a family of entrepreneurs. Haddad's athletic career began at a young age, with a focus on track and field events. He represented Lebanon in several international competitions, including the Pan American Games and the World Athletics Championships. In 2015, Haddad was selected as a UN Environment Programme (UNEP) Young Champion of the Earth, recognizing his efforts to promote sustainable development and climate action. He has since become a prominent voice on climate change, advocating for policy reforms and sustainable practices. Haddad's work extends beyond his athletic achievements, as he has also co-founded several social enterprises, including a sustainable energy company and a social impact fund. He has received numerous awards for his contributions to social entrepreneurship and climate activism, including the 2020 Prince of Asturias Award for Social Cohesion. Through his work, Haddad aims to inspire a new generation of leaders to prioritize sustainable development and climate action. He has also been recognized for his commitment to education and community development, having established several educational programs and scholarships for young people. Haddad's impact extends beyond his own country, as he has collaborated with international organizations and governments to promote climate action and sustainable development. He has also been a vocal advocate for the rights of marginalized communities, particularly in the context of climate change. Haddad's legacy will likely be remembered as a testament to the power of individual action and collective advocacy in shaping a more sustainable future.
